summary: Describes IS-IS extensions for Traffic Engineering, adding information to link state PDUs about network state for TE calculations. It is informational. It was updated by RFC 4205 and replaced by RFC 5305.

eli5.summary: Routers share maps. This adds extra details, like how much room each road has, so smarter routes can be chosen.

subtitle: New IS-IS building blocks that carry wider metrics, link bandwidth and a router ID for traffic engineering.

tldr.problem: The IS-IS neighbor and IP reachability TLVs limit a metric to the range 0-63 and carry no link details such as bandwidth, which traffic engineering needs.
tldr.mechanism: It defines three new TLVs (extended IS reachability, extended IP reachability and TE router ID) and introduces sub-TLVs, which sit inside a TLV and carry per-link details like bandwidth and administrative groups.
tldr.outcome: RFC 3784 is Informational, was updated by RFC 4205, and was obsoleted by RFC 5305, which is where the current definition lives.

today: RFC 3784 is Informational. It was updated by RFC 4205 and obsoleted by RFC 5305, so the current definition of these IS-IS traffic engineering extensions is in the newer document.

sections.title: Introduction and Sub-TLVs
sections.content:
Each IS-IS router (Intermediate System) advertises Link State Protocol Data Units (LSPs). An LSP has a fixed header and a number of TLVs: tuples of Type, Length and Value. This document designs new TLVs to replace the existing IS Neighbor TLV and IP Reachability TLV and to add link characteristics needed for traffic engineering. Secondary goals are a larger metric range and better encoding of IP prefixes. Migration to the new TLVs is not discussed.

It also introduces sub-TLVs. They work like TLVs, but exist inside a TLV instead of inside a packet. Each has a one-octet Type, a one-octet Length and zero or more octets of Value. Unknown sub-TLVs are ignored and skipped upon receipt. New sub-TLV types are allocated after review on the IS-IS mailing list.
sections.eli5: Each router passes around small labelled boxes of facts. Now a box can hold smaller boxes inside it for extra details.

sections.title: The Extended IS Reachability TLV
sections.content:
This is TLV type 22. The old IS reachability TLV (type 2) gives a metric of just 6 usable bits, so a range of 0-63, and spends 11 octets per neighbor on fields that are not commonly used. The new structure has 7 octets of system ID and pseudonode number, 3 octets of default metric, 1 octet for the length of sub-TLVs, and 0-244 octets of sub-TLVs. Without sub-TLVs it still takes 11 octets and fits up to 23 neighbors in one TLV.

The metric is a 24-bit unsigned integer, while the new IP reachability metric is 32 bits, chosen so that an intra-area cost is very unlikely to be chopped off when it becomes an inter-area route. Metrics greater than or equal to MAX_PATH_METRIC are treated as MAX_PATH_METRIC, set to 4,261,412,864 (0xFE000000). A link advertised with the maximum link metric (2^24 - 1) MUST NOT be used in the normal SPF computation, so it can be available to traffic engineering without being used for hop-by-hop routing.
sections.eli5: The old note only had room for a tiny number for how costly a road is. The new note has room for a much bigger number.

sections.title: The Traffic Engineering Sub-TLVs
sections.content:
Several sub-TLVs describe a link. Bandwidth values are 32-bit IEEE floating point numbers in bytes (not bits) per second.

  • 3, Administrative group (color): a 4-octet bit mask set by the administrator. The least significant bit is group 0 and the most significant is group 31.
  • 6 and 8, IPv4 interface and neighbor address: routers that implement traffic engineering MUST include sub-TLV 6, and sub-TLV 8 on point-to-point adjacencies. Implementations MUST NOT inject a /32 prefix for these addresses into routing or forwarding tables, because that can cause forwarding loops with systems that do not support the sub-TLV.
  • 9, Maximum link bandwidth, and 10, Reservable link bandwidth: reservable bandwidth can exceed the link speed for oversubscription.
  • 11, Unreserved bandwidth: eight values, one for each setup priority 0 through 7. Rapid changes SHOULD NOT cause rapid generation of LSPs.
  • 18, TE Default metric: a 24-bit value for traffic engineering SPF. Without it, the normal default metric MUST be used.
sections.eli5: Extra notes about each road: how many lanes it has in total, how many are still free, and a colour tag the boss gave it.

sections.title: Extended IP Reachability and the Router ID
sections.content:
The extended IP reachability TLV is type 135. It has a 4-octet (32-bit) metric and one control octet: an up/down bit, a bit saying sub-TLVs are present, and 6 bits of prefix length. The prefix then takes 0 to 4 octets, using the minimum needed for its length. This document defines no sub-TLVs for it.

The up/down bit prevents loops when prefixes move between levels. It is 0 when a prefix is first injected, and MUST be set to 1 when a prefix is advertised from a higher level to a lower one, such as level 2 to level 1. A prefix with the bit set to 1 may only be advertised further down. It is also set to 1 when a prefix passes between areas at the same level.

The Traffic Engineering router ID TLV is type 134. It carries the 4-octet router ID of the originating router, a single stable address that can be used to reference the router regardless of its interface state. A router that implements traffic engineering MUST include it. If the router uses a BGP router ID, the TE router ID SHOULD be the same.
sections.eli5: A small flag on each route says whether it has already gone downhill. Routes that went downhill are never allowed to climb back, so they cannot go round in circles.

sections.title: IANA and Security
sections.content:
IANA recorded the three new TLV types (22, 134 and 135), all valid in LSPs only. It also created a registry of sub-TLVs for TLV 22, with the range 0-255 and allocations requiring documentation and Designated Expert approval, and an empty registry for sub-TLVs of TLV 135.

The security section is a single sentence: the document raises no new security issues for IS-IS.
sections.eli5: The numbers for the new boxes were written in an official list, so nobody else reuses them. The authors say nothing new is risky here.
